experiments.system: Transformer (Transformer-tiny (2 encoder / 2 decoder layers), trained from scratch, following ref [33]'s STMC-Transformer baseline recipe (Section IV-A2: "we follow [33] to train a Transformer-tiny model with 2 encoder layers and 2 decoder layers"); hyperparameters per Table 5's Transformer-tiny column (lr 7e-4, inverse_sqrt schedule, Adam beta (0.9,0.98), warmup 2000, label-smoothing 0.1, dropout 0.3, batch-size 2048).)
experiments.checkpoint_rule: CORRECTION 2026-09-01: Table 5 is captioned by the paper itself as 'Hyperparameters of transformer models used in Section III' -- it does not apply to Table 6. Section IV-A2 only says the Transformer baseline "follows [33]" without restating specific hyperparameters for Table 6. Resolved by using ref [33]'s own documented sample recipe (kayoyin/transformer-slt README Sample Usage section) verbatim -- the least-invasive interpretation of "follow [33]" -- rather than the earlier (incorrect) assumption that Table 5 applies here. This includes ref [33]'s own early-stopping criterion, so no epoch/step count needs to be guessed for this baseline, unlike mBART/mT5. Checkpoint selection: ref [33]'s own -early_stopping 3 -early_stopping_criteria accuracy ppl.

experiments.system: +Back-translation (Transformer-tiny + back-translation augmentation: a Transformer-tiny text-to-gloss model is trained and used to translate 30K in-domain (weather-forecast-domain) German sentences from Section III-C into synthetic gloss, which augments the gloss-to-text training data (Section IV-A2).)

Batch size / step budget for mBART/mT5 finetuning are not stated by the paper. First full run (mt5-small/phoenix, batch_size=16, epochs=10 -> 4440 total steps) produced near-zero BLEU. Root-cause diagnosis via per-step loss tracing (not a code bug): the paper-specified warmup_steps=2500 consumed 56% of Phoenix2014T's 4440-step budget at epochs=10, leaving too few high-LR steps to converge on the smallest dataset (loss did fall 50->12 but not enough for fluent output). RESOLVED with a fixed uniform step budget across all three datasets: max_steps=40000, eval/save every 4000 steps, batch_size=16 (all still undocumented by the paper). This keeps warmup at 6.25% of training for every dataset instead of varying 8%-56% by dataset size. Verified via extended loss tracing (3000 steps) that loss keeps falling well past warmup completion, supporting this fix.

Decoding/inference settings for the mBART/mT5 systems are not stated by the paper. First full runs at default generation config (no explicit num_beams/no_repeat_ngram_size) produced fluent but degenerate, repetition-looped text for mT5 checkpoints (verified directly via modal_app.py::inspect_checkpoint on real weights: e.g. 'und nun die wettervorhersage fur morgen' repeated many times), causing near-zero BLEU despite falling loss; mBART was not observed to collapse this way. Fixed by setting model.generation_config.num_beams=4 and no_repeat_ngram_size=3 uniformly for every system (standard defaults, and num_beams=4 matches ref [33]'s own translate.py beam_size=4 usage for this benchmark family). Re-evaluated already-finished checkpoints (mbart-csldaily, mt5-small-csldaily) from their saved weights under the fixed config rather than retraining.

Ref [33]'s tools/rouge.py strips all non-ASCII characters (REMOVE_CHAR_PATTERN=[^A-Za-z0-9]) before scoring, which empties CSL-Daily's Chinese text entirely (rouge-l=0.0 observed for both mbart-csldaily and mt5-small-csldaily regardless of translation quality). Immaterial to this reproduction: Table 6 does not report ROUGE-L/METEOR for CSL-Daily (only BLEU-1..4), so no target depends on this tool limitation; noted for completeness.

mT5 systems substantially underperform mBART and the paper's reported mT5 numbers on Phoenix2014T/ASLG-PC12 (much less so on CSL-Daily). Verified this is not the earlier repetition bug: generated text is fluent, grammatical, non-repeating German, but shows mode collapse to generic weather-forecast templates ('und nun die wettervorhersage fur morgen X') rather than gloss-specific translation, i.e. genuine undertraining/underfitting relative to mBART at the same step budget, not a decoding artifact (verified via modal_app.py::inspect_checkpoint on real checkpoint-40000 weights, 2026-08-31). One concrete, unavoidable implementation asymmetry: T5Config exposes only a single dropout_rate (set to the paper's 0.3), with no separate attention-dropout parameter, whereas mBART's BartConfig lets attention_dropout=0.1 be set separately as the paper specifies. mT5 therefore trains with ~3x higher effective attention dropout than mBART in this reproduction, a plausible contributing cause not chosen for tuning purposes. Not further adjusted to chase the published mT5 numbers, per policy (never tune toward the published score).
